entries.title: Artificer
entries.body:
# Artificer

## Overview
# Class Overview

The Artificer is a master inventor, engineer, researcher, and creator who blends magic, science, craftsmanship, and innovation into a single discipline. Unlike traditional spellcasters who channel magic through faith, instinct, or study alone, Artificers view magic as a resource to be understood, refined, and engineered.

Where a Wizard studies spells, an Artificer studies systems.

Through experimentation and invention, Artificers create gadgets, constructs, enchanted equipment, dimensional technologies, alchemical compounds, and soul-powered creations capable of reshaping the world around them. Their workshops produce wonders that many consider impossible, while their inventions often blur the line between magic and technology.

Artificers are natural problem-solvers. Every challenge presents an opportunity for innovation. Every obstacle is simply a puzzle waiting to be solved.

Whether constructing mechanical companions, crafting legendary artifacts, manipulating matter itself through Arcane Exchange, or carrying entire buildings in their pockets, Artificers are defined by one principle:

> If it does not exist, build it.

## Class Identity

The Artificer excels through preparation, creativity, and invention rather than direct magical power.

### Primary Roles

- Crafter
- Inventor
- Enchanter
- Researcher
- Support Specialist
- Resource Manager
- Utility Expert

### Secondary Roles

- Construct Commander
- Battlefield Controller
- Alchemist
- Engineer
- Explorer

## Artificer Motto

> "Magic is not a mystery. It is a system waiting to be understood."

## Talent Tree
Talent pathways live in the talent folders for this class. Each talent has its own page under `talents/tier-*`.

## Lore
# Origins of the Artificers

Long before the modern age, magic was viewed as a force to be worshipped, feared, or studied. Few considered building with it.

The earliest Artificers were craftsmen, miners, alchemists, blacksmiths, and scholars who became frustrated by the limitations of conventional magic. While Wizards debated theory and Clerics sought divine guidance, these pioneers sought practical solutions.

They asked questions others ignored: why cast the same spell every day when a device could perform the task indefinitely, why rely on magical talent alone when power could be stored, and why learn a spell when a machine could replicate its effect?

## The First Innovators

The first true Artificers appeared during the Age of Discovery. These individuals began combining smithing, enchanting, alchemy, runecraft, engineering, and arcane theory into a new field of study.

The earliest inventions were simple: self-heating cookware, enchanted lanterns, automated pumps, and reinforced tools. Over time these creations became more ambitious, eventually producing devices capable of rivaling spellcasters.

## The Great Debate

The rise of the Artificers sparked controversy across Asteria. Traditional scholars argued that magic should be studied. Artificers argued that magic should be used. Traditional enchanters argued that magic is sacred. Artificers argued that magic is a resource.

## The Age of Invention

As Artifice spread throughout the world, entire industries emerged around Artificer creations: arcane lighting systems, mana-powered tools, mechanical transports, automated workshops, and dimensional storage devices.

Many cities owe their growth to inventions developed by Artificers. Some kingdoms owe their survival to them. Others blame them for countless disasters. Both are often correct.

## The Soul Revolution

The greatest breakthrough in Artificer history came with the discovery of Soul Integration. Researchers discovered that soul energy could be captured, refined, and utilized within crafted objects.

This led to the creation of Soul-Bound Items, Arcane Reactors, Scaling Creations, Living Constructs, and Sentient Artifacts. The discovery revolutionized the profession, and also created some of its greatest dangers.

## The Philosophy of Creation

Artificers do not view creation as a finished act. Nothing is truly complete. Everything can be improved. Every invention may be refined. Every design may evolve. Every problem has a solution.

## Artificers and Society

Artificers may become master craftsmen, guild engineers, royal inventors, researchers, explorers, merchants, treasure hunters, relic seekers, dungeon delvers, monster researchers, or independent inventors.

Many travel the world searching for lost schematics, ancient technologies, rare materials, and forgotten knowledge. To an Artificer, every ruin is a library, every artifact is a lesson, and every mystery is an opportunity.

## The Artificer Creed

> We build.
>
> We improve.
>
> We discover.
>
> We create.
>
> We fail.
>
> We learn.
>
> We build again.

## Legacy

The greatest Artificers are remembered for what they leave behind: a bridge that still stands, a reactor that still burns, a construct that still walks, a fortress that still protects, or an invention that changed the world.

entries.title: Bloodhunter
entries.body:
# Bloodhunter

## Overview
The Bloodhunter is unlike any other warrior. Rather than relying solely on strength, mana, or stamina, they wield **Sangramancy**—the forbidden art of blood magic. Every technique fueled through Sangramancy draws upon the emotions carried within blood, leaving behind a lingering resonance known as **Blood Points (BP)**.

Blood Points do not represent physical blood. Instead, they represent the emotional burden accumulated through repeated use of Sangramancy. Rage, hatred, fear, sorrow, vengeance, and countless other emotions become trapped within the Bloodhunter's soul.

Learning Sangramancy is not simply mastering blood magic—it is mastering yourself.

Every Bloodhunter talent generates Blood Points unless otherwise stated.

---

# Blood Point Limit

Every Bloodhunter has a maximum Blood Point Limit representing how much emotional resonance they can safely contain before losing control.

As a Bloodhunter grows stronger, they do not generate fewer Blood Points. Instead, they learn to withstand greater emotional burdens before their mind finally fractures.

| Progression | Maximum Blood Points |
|------------|---------------------:|
| Bloodhunter | 20 BP |
| Tier II | 35 BP |
| Tier III | 50 BP |
| Tier IV | 70 BP |
| Tier V | 100 BP |

Some Bloodhunter talents and magical equipment may further increase this limit.

---

# Gaining Blood Points

Every Bloodhunter talent lists how many Blood Points it generates.

As a general guideline:

- Minor techniques generate **2–5 BP**
- Standard techniques generate **5–8 BP**
- Advanced techniques generate **8–12 BP**
- Legendary techniques generate **10–20 BP**

Blood Points are accumulated immediately after successfully activating an ability unless stated otherwise.

---

# Recovering Blood Points

Blood Points are **persistent** and do not disappear when combat ends.

### End of Combat

- Blood Points remain unchanged.

### Short Rest

- Reduce your current Blood Points by **25% (rounded up).**

### Long Rest

- Reduce your current Blood Points to **0**.

Certain Bloodhunter talents, relics, rituals, or blessings may restore additional Blood Points.

---

# Bloodlust

When a Bloodhunter's current Blood Points exceed their maximum Blood Point Limit, the emotions carried within the blood finally overwhelm their own.

The Bloodhunter immediately enters a state known as **Bloodlust**.

Bloodlust is not blind rage.

It is absolute emotional detachment.

The Bloodhunter becomes unnaturally calm. Their breathing slows. Their movements become precise. Compassion, hesitation, and mercy disappear, replaced only by an overwhelming instinct to hunt and kill.

To witness Bloodlust is to watch someone become less human with every passing moment.

---

# Effects of Bloodlust

While Bloodlust is active:

- The player immediately loses control of their character.
- The Game Master controls the Bloodhunter until Bloodlust ends.
- The Bloodhunter identifies the greatest hostile threat they can perceive and relentlessly attempts to kill it.
- The Bloodhunter ignores pain, fear, and self-preservation.
- Any creature physically preventing them from reaching their prey becomes a valid target, including allies.
- The Bloodhunter cannot willingly perform social interactions, negotiations, or acts of mercy.
- Sangramancy abilities may still be used if they aid in eliminating the chosen prey.
- Bloodlust cannot occur outside of combat.

---

# Ending Bloodlust

Bloodlust ends immediately when one of the following occurs:

- Combat ends.
- The Bloodhunter falls unconscious.
- The Bloodhunter dies.
- A powerful magical effect specifically suppresses Bloodlust.
- Another ability or talent states that it ends Bloodlust.

Once Bloodlust ends, the Bloodhunter retains their current Blood Points unless another effect removes them.

---

# Mastering Sangramancy

Every Bloodhunter walks a dangerous path.

Some spend their lives learning to increase their Blood Point Limit.

Others develop techniques to reduce Blood Point generation.

The greatest Bloodhunters are not those who possess the most power.

They are those who can stand upon the edge of Bloodlust, stare into the darkness within themselves, and choose not to fall.

---

> *"People believe blood carries life. They are wrong. Blood carries emotion... and emotion is far more dangerous."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

entries.title: Spellblade
entries.body:
# Spellblade

## Overview
# Spellblade Overview

The Spellblade is a master of both steel and sorcery, seamlessly blending martial discipline with arcane power to create a combat style unlike any other. Rather than separating swordsmanship and spellcasting, Spellblades weave the two together, empowering every strike with mana while using their weapon as the conduit through which their magic flows. Their greatest strength lies in adaptability, allowing them to transition effortlessly between close-quarters combat, ranged magical techniques, battlefield control, and defensive counterplay.

Throughout their journey, Spellblades learn to enhance their weapons, pursue fleeing enemies with supernatural speed, counter hostile spells, manipulate the battlefield through Arcane Dominion, and unleash devastating techniques such as Arcane Cut. As their mastery grows, they forge their own Arcane Arsenal, creating weapons directly from mana and reshaping them to suit any challenge. At the pinnacle of their training, legendary transformations such as Avatar of the Blade and Arcane Catalyst allow them to transcend mortal limits, becoming the ultimate expression of martial and magical harmony.

A Spellblade excels in versatility, capable of fulfilling the roles of warrior, mage, skirmisher, duelist, or battlefield commander depending on the situation. Success with the class rewards careful planning, resource management, and tactical decision-making. Every battle becomes a test of choosing the right weapon, the right spell, and the perfect moment to unleash overwhelming arcane power. Few can rival a true Spellblade, for they do not merely wield magic and steel—they become the perfect union of both.
